# Goal

Run FLAIR+ on data simulated from a fully specified data-generating model,
then quantify uncertainty for **every** estimated parameter using
`compute_UQ()` from `flair_plus_minibatch_tr.R`. For each parameter family
we report:

1. The MAP point estimate vs. the true value.
2. The 95% posterior credible interval vs. the true value (coverage check).

This document is self-contained — it is meant to be re-knit any time
`compute_UQ()` or the related C++ helper `compute_V_diag_all_cpp()` change.

---

# True data-generating model

We sample from the exact prior structure FLAIR+ targets, so that posterior
intervals can be assessed against ground truth. With
$d = q + k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\boldsymbol{\xi}_j &\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\, \mathbf{I}_H),
  \qquad j=1,\dots,p
  &(\text{trait embedding; see note below}) \\
\sigma_r^2 &\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}
  \text{InvGamma}(a_{\text{true}},\, b_{\text{true}}),
  \qquad r=1,\dots,d
  &(\text{per-dim residual scale}) \\
\kappa_r^2 &\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}
  \text{InvGamma}(c_{\text{true}},\, d_{\text{true}}),
  \qquad r=1,\dots,d
  &(\text{per-row Gamma scale}) \\
\Gamma_{r,h} &\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,\, \kappa_r^2)
  &(\text{trait-to-param map}) \\
\boldsymbol{\mu}_j &= \Gamma\, \boldsymbol{\xi}_j
  &(\text{structured prior mean of }\tilde\beta_j) \\
\tilde\beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_j,\,
  \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\dots,\sigma_d^2))
  &(\text{species coefficients}) \\
\tilde\beta_j &= (\beta_j^\top, \lambda_j^\top)^\top
  \in \mathbb{R}^q \times \mathbb{R}^k
  &(\text{covariate / latent split}) \\
\boldsymbol{\eta}_i &\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\, \mathbf{I}_k / k)
  &(\text{latent site scores}) \\
y_{ij} &\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}\!\left(
  \sigma(\mathbf{x}_i^\top \beta_j + \boldsymbol{\eta}_i^\top \lambda_j) \right)
  &(\text{binary outcome})
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r dgm-params}
set.seed(2026)

n  <- 200L   # sites
p  <- 120L   # species (large enough for stable Gamma posterior)
q  <- 3L     # covariates (col 1 = intercept)
k  <- 3L     # latent factors
H  <- 20L    # trait-embedding dimension (matches real-data diffusion h=20)
d  <- q + k

# Embedding scale. With xi_j ~ N(0, I_H) the coefficient signal
# Var(mu_jr) = kappa_r^2 * ||xi_j||^2 grows like kappa^2 * H, saturating the
# logistic at large H. Scaling xi by sqrt(4/H) fixes E||xi_j||^2 = 4, holding
# the linear-predictor signal at the H=4 regime (sd(Z) ~ 5.4) so only the trait
# dimension changes. Reduces to 1 at H=4 (backward-consistent).
xi_scale <- sqrt(4 / H)

# Hyperparameters match the fitter defaults (get_init_plus: a=3,b=2,c=3,d=2)
# so the prior is correctly specified. IG(3,2): mode = b/(a+1) = 0.5, mean = 1.0.
# IG(3, 1/2): mean 1/4. With unit scales the linear predictor has sd about 6
# and the effective counts m_j = sum_i phi''(z_ij) fall to 5-20 even at n=200,
# outside the common-species regime of the theory; at mean 1/4 the predictor
# has sd about 3 and m_j/n is about 0.12.
a_true <- 3;  b_true <- 0.5   # IG(3,0.5): mean sigma^2 = b/(a-1) = 0.25
c_true <- 3;  d_true <- 0.5   # IG(3,0.5): mean kappa^2 = d/(c-1) = 0.25

# Draw scale parameters from their priors
sigma_sq_true <- 1 / rgamma(d, shape = a_true, rate = b_true)   # length d
kappa_sq_true <- 1 / rgamma(d, shape = c_true, rate = d_true)   # length d

# Trait embedding (rows = embedding dims, cols = species)
Xi_mat <- matrix(rnorm(H * p), H, p) * xi_scale                # H x p

# Gamma: row r drawn from N(0, kappa_sq_true[r] * I_H)
Gamma_0 <- matrix(rnorm(d * H), d, H) *
           matrix(sqrt(kappa_sq_true), d, H, byrow = FALSE)     # d x H

# Species coefficients: Beta_Lambda_j ~ N(Gamma * xi_j, diag(sigma_sq_true))
Mu_0     <- t(Gamma_0 %*% Xi_mat)                                # p x d
Delta_0  <- matrix(rnorm(p * d), p, d) *
            matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p, d, byrow = TRUE)
BL_0     <- Mu_0 + Delta_0
Beta_0   <- BL_0[, seq_len(q),           drop = FALSE]
Lambda_0 <- BL_0[, q + seq_len(k),       drop = FALSE]

# Site design and outcome
X     <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n * (q - 1)), n, q - 1))
Eta_0 <- matrix(rnorm(n * k), n, k) / sqrt(k)
Z_0   <- X %*% t(Beta_0) + Eta_0 %*% t(Lambda_0)
P_0   <- 1 / (1 + exp(-Z_0))
# Canonical truth: post-processing makes the factors orthogonal to X, which moves
# Eta_0 A_0 (A_0 = (X'X)^{-1} X'Eta_0) into the intercept and slopes: beta + A_0 lambda,
# and correspondingly Gamma[1:q,] + A_0 Gamma[q+1:k,]. Coverage of FLAIR/FLAIR++ uses these.
A_0      <- solve(crossprod(X), crossprod(X, Eta_0))
Beta_0c  <- Beta_0 + Lambda_0 %*% t(A_0)
Gamma_0c <- Gamma_0[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE] + A_0 %*% Gamma_0[q + seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE]
Y     <- matrix(rbinom(n * p, 1, P_0), n, p)
colnames(Y) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p))   # required for stage-2 backbone transfer

cat(sprintf("n=%d  p=%d  q=%d  k=%d  H=%d  d=%d  marginal P(Y=1) = %.3f\n",
            n, p, q, k, H, d, mean(Y)))
cat(sprintf("True sigma_sq range: [%.3f, %.3f]   mean=%.3f\n",
            min(sigma_sq_true), max(sigma_sq_true), mean(sigma_sq_true)))
cat(sprintf("True kappa_sq range: [%.3f, %.3f]   mean=%.3f\n",
            min(kappa_sq_true), max(kappa_sq_true), mean(kappa_sq_true)))
```

---

# Marginal variance verification

Marginalising Γ out of the hierarchical prior gives, for each species $j$ and
dimension $r$:
$$
\operatorname{Var}(\tilde{b}_{jr}) = \sigma_r^2 + \kappa_r^2\,\|\xi_j\|^2 .
$$
We verify this holds empirically by drawing `r N_rep <- 500L; N_rep` independent
realisations of $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ from the DGM (keeping $\Xi$, $\sigma^2$,
$\kappa^2$ fixed at the values drawn above) and comparing the sample variance to
the closed-form formula.

**Hyperparameters.** The DGM and fitter share $a=3, b=1/2, c=3, d=1/2$, so the
prior is correctly specified. Both give $\text{InvGamma}(3,1/2)$ with mode 1/8 and
mean 1/4 for each dimension of $\sigma^2$ and $\kappa^2$; with mean 1 the linear
predictor saturates (sd about 6, $m_j/n \approx 0.07$) and no Gaussian
approximation is calibrated.

```{r dgm-margvar-check, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
N_rep   <- 500L
xi_sq   <- colSums(Xi_mat^2)           # p-vector: ||xi_j||^2

# Theoretical marginal variance: Var(BL_{jr}) = sigma_sq_true[r] + kappa_sq_true[r] * ||xi_j||^2
BL_theo_var <- outer(xi_sq, kappa_sq_true) +
               matrix(sigma_sq_true, p, d, byrow = TRUE)

# Sample N_rep independent BL matrices from the DGM (Xi fixed)
set.seed(2026 + 99)
BL_rep <- array(NA_real_, c(p, d, N_rep))
for (s in seq_len(N_rep)) {
  G_s    <- matrix(rnorm(d * H), d, H) *
            matrix(sqrt(kappa_sq_true), d, H, byrow = FALSE)
  Mu_s   <- t(G_s %*% Xi_mat)
  De_s   <- matrix(rnorm(p * d), p, d) *
            matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p, d, byrow = TRUE)
  BL_rep[,, s] <- Mu_s + De_s
}
BL_emp_var <- apply(BL_rep, c(1L, 2L), var)  # p x d

cat(sprintf("Empirical vs theoretical BL marginal variance (%d reps):\n", N_rep))
cat(sprintf("  Pearson correlation : %.4f  (expect ≈ 1)\n",
            cor(as.vector(BL_emp_var), as.vector(BL_theo_var))))
cat(sprintf("  Mean ratio emp/theo : %.4f  (expect ≈ 1)\n",
            mean(BL_emp_var / BL_theo_var)))
cat(sprintf("  Theoretical range   : [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            min(BL_theo_var), max(BL_theo_var)))
cat(sprintf("  Empirical range     : [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            min(BL_emp_var), max(BL_emp_var)))

par(mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
plot(as.vector(BL_theo_var), as.vector(BL_emp_var),
     xlab = expression(paste("Theoretical  ", Var(tilde(b)[jr]),
                             " = ", sigma[r]^2 + kappa[r]^2 * ~group("||", xi[j], "||")^2)),
     ylab = "Empirical variance (500 DGM samples)",
     pch  = 16, col  = rgb(0, 0.4, 0.8, 0.3))
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
title(sprintf("DGM marginal variance check  (r=%.4f)",
              cor(as.vector(BL_emp_var), as.vector(BL_theo_var))))
```

# Fitting configuration

We use the trust-region minibatch wrapper. The DGM and fitter share prior
hyperparameters $a=3, b=1/2, c=3, d=1/2$ (prior mean $\sigma^2=\kappa^2=1/4$)
so the prior is correctly specified.

```{r fit-config}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Rcpp)
  library(RcppArmadillo)
})
source(file.path(FLAIR_CODE_DIR, "flair_plus_minibatch_tr.R"))

fit_cfg <- list(
  iter_max_pretrain     = 5L,
  iter_max_train        = 200L,
  tol                   = 1e-4,
  loss_tol              = 1e-5,   # tighter: 1e-3 caused premature exit after ~1 training iter
  cores                 = 4L,
  do_post_process       = TRUE,
  randomized_svd        = FALSE,
  timing_diagnostics    = FALSE,
  m_prior_var           = 1 / k,
  max_embedding_dim     = H,
  b = b_true, d_hyp = d_true          # inverse-gamma rates matching the DGM
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(name = names(fit_cfg),
             value = vapply(fit_cfg, function(x) format(x, nsmall = 0), character(1))),
  caption = "Fitting configuration"
)
```

```{r run-fit}
t0 <- proc.time()
fit <- do.call(FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper,
               c(list(Y = Y, X = X, Xi_mat = Xi_mat, k = k,
                      Y_all = Y, Xi_all = Xi_mat),   # enables stage-2 training loop
                 fit_cfg))
fit_time <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]
cat(sprintf("Fit elapsed: %.2f s\n", fit_time))

H_eff  <- ncol(fit$Gamma)
Xi_eff <- Xi_mat[seq_len(H_eff), , drop = FALSE]
```

# Posterior uncertainty for every parameter

We compute two UQ tiers and compare them throughout:

* **`uq` (plug-in)**: `compute_UQ()` — Beta/Lambda Laplace at fixed Γ,
  σ², M; sigma_sq via conjugate InvGamma conditional on BL.
* **`uq_m` (marginal)**: `compute_UQ_joint()` — Beta/Lambda covariance from the
  Schur complement over the site factors M, plus Γ propagation; Γ marginalised
  over σ² by Monte Carlo; σ² via the REML-corrected InvGamma.

```{r run-uq}
t0 <- proc.time()
uq   <- compute_UQ(fit, Y, X, Xi_mat = Xi_eff, alpha = 0.05)
uq_time_cond <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]

t0 <- proc.time()
uq_m <- compute_UQ_joint(fit, Y, X, Xi_mat = Xi_eff, alpha = 0.05)
uq_time_marg <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]

cat(sprintf("UQ (plug-in)  elapsed: %.2f s\n", uq_time_cond))
cat(sprintf("UQ (marginal) elapsed: %.2f s\n", uq_time_marg))
uq_time <- uq_time_cond + uq_time_marg
```

Summary of returned posterior dispersion per parameter family:

```{r uq-overview}
qsumm <- function(x) c(
  min    = min(x,    na.rm = TRUE),
  median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean   = mean(x,   na.rm = TRUE),
  max    = max(x,    na.rm = TRUE)
)
sd_summary <- rbind(
  Beta     = qsumm(uq$Beta$sd),
  Lambda   = qsumm(uq$Lambda$sd),
  M        = qsumm(uq$M$sd),
  Gamma    = qsumm(uq$Gamma$sd),
  sigma_sq = qsumm(uq$sigma_sq$sd),
  kappa_sq = qsumm(uq$kappa_sq$sd)
)
knitr::kable(round(sd_summary, 4),
             caption = "Posterior SD summary (95% CIs use these via N(0,1) quantile)")
```

# Results

**Observational status of X and Ξ.** The covariate matrix $X$ ($n\times q$) is
observed data, fully known. The trait-embedding matrix $\Xi$ ($H\times p$)
represents species traits (e.g., body size, diet); in this simulation the true
$\Xi$ is drawn once from $\mathcal{N}(0,I_H)$ and used as the fixed prior mean
passed to the fitter. The current wrapper treats $\Xi$ as fixed (no update step
for $\Xi$), which is appropriate when traits are observed without error.

**Trait covariance — simulation vs. real data.**
Drawing $\xi_j \stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, I_H)$ is equivalent to
assuming a **star phylogeny**: $\mathrm{Cov}(\xi_i, \xi_j) = 0$ for all $i \neq j$,
i.e.\ no cross-species trait correlation.
This is the *hardest* case for estimating $\Gamma$: with no phylogenetic signal,
each species contributes an independent, unshrunk draw to the BL regression,
so $\hat\Gamma$ converges at the usual $O(1/\sqrt{p})$ rate with no
between-species borrowing.

In real data we use a taxonomic/phylogenetic tree.
The covariance matrix $\Sigma_{\text{phylo}}$ is obtained from the tree via
a Brownian-motion kernel: $[\Sigma_{\text{phylo}}]_{ij} =$ shared branch length
from the root to the most recent common ancestor of species $i$ and $j$
(Grafen branch-length scaling in our coral data; see `compare3.R` lines 404--413).
The true trait distribution becomes
$\Xi \sim \mathcal{MN}(0,\, I_H \otimes \Sigma_{\text{phylo}})$,
meaning closely-related species have nearly identical trait vectors
and effectively count as a single species for $\Gamma$ estimation.
**Strong phylogenetic structure therefore makes $\hat\Gamma$ harder, not easier**
(fewer effective independent data points), but also tightens the prior on $\beta_j$
for rare/new species (the key application benefit).

Procrustes helpers (rotation-tied families only):

```{r procrustes-helpers}
procrustes_R <- function(L0, Lhat) {
  sv <- svd(crossprod(Lhat, L0))
  sv$u %*% t(sv$v)
}
R              <- procrustes_R(Lambda_0, fit$Lambda)
Lambda_aligned <- fit$Lambda %*% R
M_aligned      <- fit$M      %*% R
emp_rmse       <- function(est, truth)
  sqrt(mean((as.vector(est) - as.vector(truth))^2))
coverage <- function(lo, hi, truth) {
  ok <- is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(lo[ok] <= truth[ok] & truth[ok] <= hi[ok])
}
ci_width <- function(lo, hi) mean(hi - lo, na.rm = TRUE)
sig_q <- seq_len(q)   # index of Beta-associated sigma_sq / kappa_sq dims
```

```{r convergence-compute, cache=TRUE, include=FALSE}
# cache-key: pred_mzsq_Gam per-row formula 2026-06-16, n=800, loss_tol=1e-5, iter_max_train=100
p_cv <- 60L
set.seed(2026 + 77)

Xi_cv    <- matrix(rnorm(H * p_cv), H, p_cv) * xi_scale
Gamma_cv <- matrix(rnorm(d * H), d, H) *
            matrix(sqrt(kappa_sq_true), d, H, byrow = FALSE)
BL_cv    <- t(Gamma_cv %*% Xi_cv) +
            matrix(rnorm(p_cv * d), p_cv, d) *
            matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p_cv, d, byrow = TRUE)
Beta_cv  <- BL_cv[, seq_len(q),     drop = FALSE]
Lam_cv   <- BL_cv[, q + seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]

n_vals <- c(50L, 100L, 200L, 400L, 800L)

conv_rows <- lapply(n_vals, function(n_cv) {
  set.seed(2026 + n_cv)
  X_cv   <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n_cv * (q - 1)), n_cv, q - 1))
  Eta_cv <- matrix(rnorm(n_cv * k), n_cv, k) / sqrt(k)
  A_cv      <- solve(crossprod(X_cv), crossprod(X_cv, Eta_cv))
  Beta_cv_c <- Beta_cv + Lam_cv %*% t(A_cv)
  Gam_cv_c  <- Gamma_cv[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE] + A_cv %*% Gamma_cv[q + seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE]
  Z_cv   <- X_cv %*% t(Beta_cv) + Eta_cv %*% t(Lam_cv)
  Y_cv   <- matrix(rbinom(n_cv * p_cv, 1, plogis(Z_cv)), n_cv, p_cv)
  colnames(Y_cv) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p_cv))

  fit_cv <- FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper(
    Y_cv, X_cv, Xi_cv, k,
    Y_all = Y_cv, Xi_all = Xi_cv,
    iter_max_pretrain = 5L, iter_max_train = 100L, loss_tol = 1e-5,
    max_embedding_dim = H, cores = fit_cfg$cores,
    timing_diagnostics = FALSE, b = b_true, d_hyp = d_true)
  He <- ncol(fit_cv$Gamma)
  Xi_cv_He <- Xi_cv[seq_len(He), , drop = FALSE]

  err_Beta       <- emp_rmse(fit_cv$Beta, Beta_cv)
  err_Gam_q      <- emp_rmse(fit_cv$Gamma[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)],
                              Gamma_cv[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)])
  err_sig_q      <- emp_rmse(fit_cv$sigma_sq[sig_q], sigma_sq_true[sig_q])
  err_sig_q_reml <- emp_rmse(
    compute_sigma_sq_reml(fit_cv, Y_cv, X_cv, Xi_cv_He)[sig_q],
    sigma_sq_true[sig_q])
  err_Lam_RI     <- emp_rmse(tcrossprod(fit_cv$Lambda) / k,
                              tcrossprod(Lam_cv)        / k)

  uq_c_cv <- compute_UQ(fit_cv, Y_cv, X_cv, Xi_mat = Xi_cv_He, alpha = 0.05)
  uq_m_cv <- compute_UQ_joint(fit_cv, Y_cv, X_cv, Xi_mat = Xi_cv_He, alpha = 0.05)

  cov_Beta_c <- coverage(uq_c_cv$Beta$ci_lower, uq_c_cv$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_cv_c)
  cov_Beta_m <- coverage(uq_m_cv$Beta$ci_lower, uq_m_cv$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_cv_c)
  cov_Gam_m  <- coverage(
    uq_m_cv$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)],
    uq_m_cv$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)],
    Gam_cv_c[, seq_len(He)])
  cov_sig_m  <- coverage(
    uq_m_cv$sigma_sq$ci_lower[sig_q],
    uq_m_cv$sigma_sq$ci_upper[sig_q],
    sigma_sq_true[sig_q])

  mz2_fn <- function(map_mat, truth_mat, sd_mat) {
    z <- (as.vector(map_mat) - as.vector(truth_mat)) / as.vector(sd_mat)
    mean(z^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  mzsq_Beta <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$Beta, Beta_cv_c, uq_m_cv$Beta$sd)
  mzsq_Gam  <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$Gamma[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)],
                       Gam_cv_c[, seq_len(He)],
                       uq_m_cv$Gamma$sd[seq_len(q), seq_len(He)])
  mzsq_sig  <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$sigma_sq[sig_q], sigma_sq_true[sig_q],
                       uq_m_cv$sigma_sq$sd[sig_q])
  mzsq_kap  <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$kappa_sq[seq_len(q)], kappa_sq_true[seq_len(q)],
                       uq_m_cv$kappa_sq$sd[seq_len(q)])

  R_cv        <- procrustes_R(Lam_cv, fit_cv$Lambda)
  R_M_cv      <- procrustes_R(Eta_cv, fit_cv$M)
  lo_Lam_c_cv <- pmin(uq_c_cv$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_cv, uq_c_cv$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_cv)
  hi_Lam_c_cv <- pmax(uq_c_cv$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_cv, uq_c_cv$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_cv)
  lo_Lam_m_cv <- pmin(uq_m_cv$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_cv, uq_m_cv$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_cv)
  hi_Lam_m_cv <- pmax(uq_m_cv$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_cv, uq_m_cv$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_cv)
  mzsq_Lam    <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$Lambda %*% R_cv, Lam_cv, uq_m_cv$Lambda$sd)
  mzsq_M      <- mz2_fn(fit_cv$M %*% R_M_cv, Eta_cv, uq_m_cv$M$sd)
  cov_Lam_c   <- coverage(lo_Lam_c_cv, hi_Lam_c_cv, Lam_cv)
  cov_Lam_m   <- coverage(lo_Lam_m_cv, hi_Lam_m_cv, Lam_cv)
  cov_kap_m   <- coverage(uq_m_cv$kappa_sq$ci_lower[seq_len(q)],
                           uq_m_cv$kappa_sq$ci_upper[seq_len(q)],
                           kappa_sq_true[seq_len(q)])
  sig_bias  <- mean(fit_cv$sigma_sq[sig_q]) / mean(sigma_sq_true[sig_q])

  x_theo <- sqrt(d * log(n_cv * p_cv) / n_cv)

  data.frame(n = n_cv, inv_sqrt_n = 1/sqrt(n_cv), x_theo = x_theo,
             rmse_Beta = err_Beta, rmse_Gamma_q = err_Gam_q,
             rmse_Lambda_RI = err_Lam_RI,
             rmse_sigma_orig = err_sig_q, rmse_sigma_reml = err_sig_q_reml,
             cov_Beta_c = cov_Beta_c, cov_Beta_m = cov_Beta_m,
             cov_Gam_m = cov_Gam_m, cov_sig_m = cov_sig_m,
             cov_kap_m = cov_kap_m, cov_Lam_c = cov_Lam_c, cov_Lam_m = cov_Lam_m,
             mzsq_Beta = mzsq_Beta, mzsq_Gam = mzsq_Gam,
             mzsq_sig = mzsq_sig, mzsq_kap = mzsq_kap,
             mzsq_Lam = mzsq_Lam, mzsq_M = mzsq_M,
             sig_bias = sig_bias,
             pred_mzsq_Gam = mean(sigma_sq_true[sig_q] / fit_cv$sigma_sq[sig_q]),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
conv_tab <- do.call(rbind, conv_rows)
```

## Replicate-averaged coverage for β, Λ, Γ

The sweep above uses a single fit per $n$, so its $\Gamma$/$\kappa^2$ coverage is
dominated by one-draw noise. Here we hold $\Gamma_{cv}$ fixed and redraw, in
each of 20 replicates per $n$, the trait residuals of BL (assumption (B6) of
the paper), the design $X$, the latent scores $\eta$ and the outcome $Y$.
Coverage of $\beta$ is evaluated against the canonical truth
$\beta + \Lambda C^\top$, $C = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top\eta$, which is the
estimand after the post-processing $M \perp X$; it differs from the generating
$\beta$ by $O(n^{-1/2})$. Only the three rotation-tractable families are
reported: $\beta$, $\Lambda$ (oracle Procrustes), $\Gamma_{[1:q,]}$.

```{r coverage-replicate, cache=TRUE, dependson="convergence-compute", include=FALSE}
R_cov <- 20L                          # datasets averaged per n
n_cov <- c(100L, 200L, 400L, 800L)

cov_rep_rows <- lapply(n_cov, function(n_r) {
  acc <- matrix(NA_real_, R_cov, 4,
                dimnames = list(NULL, c("bpi", "bm", "Om", "Gm")))
  for (r in seq_len(R_cov)) {
    set.seed(10000L * r + n_r)
    # (B6): redraw the trait residuals of BL around the fixed Gamma_cv
    BL_r   <- t(Gamma_cv %*% Xi_cv) +
              matrix(rnorm(p_cv * d), p_cv, d) *
              matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p_cv, d, byrow = TRUE)
    Beta_r <- BL_r[, seq_len(q),     drop = FALSE]
    Lam_r  <- BL_r[, q + seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]
    X_r   <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n_r * (q - 1)), n_r, q - 1))
    Eta_r <- matrix(rnorm(n_r * k), n_r, k) / sqrt(k)
    # canonical truth (M orthogonal to X after post-processing): beta + Lambda C^T
    A_r    <- solve(crossprod(X_r), crossprod(X_r, Eta_r))
    Beta_c <- Beta_r + Lam_r %*% t(A_r)
    Gam_c  <- Gamma_cv[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE] + A_r %*% Gamma_cv[q + seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE]
    Z_r   <- X_r %*% t(Beta_r) + Eta_r %*% t(Lam_r)
    Y_r   <- matrix(rbinom(n_r * p_cv, 1, plogis(Z_r)), n_r, p_cv)
    colnames(Y_r) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p_cv))

    fit_r <- FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper(
      Y_r, X_r, Xi_cv, k, Y_all = Y_r, Xi_all = Xi_cv,
      iter_max_pretrain = 5L, iter_max_train = 100L, loss_tol = 1e-5,
      max_embedding_dim = H, cores = fit_cfg$cores, timing_diagnostics = FALSE,
      b = b_true, d_hyp = d_true)
    He_r <- ncol(fit_r$Gamma)
    Xi_r <- Xi_cv[seq_len(He_r), , drop = FALSE]

    uq_c_r <- compute_UQ(fit_r, Y_r, X_r, Xi_mat = Xi_r, alpha = 0.05)
    uq_m_r <- compute_UQ_joint(fit_r, Y_r, X_r, Xi_mat = Xi_r, alpha = 0.05)

    # Omega = Lambda Lambda^T (rotation-invariant), delta method from the
    # per-species posterior covariance blocks V_BL (species blocks independent):
    # Var(Omega_{jj'}) = lam_j'^T V_j lam_j' + lam_j^T V_j' lam_j, 4x on the diagonal.
    VL_r <- lapply(uq_m_r$V_BL, function(V) V[q + seq_len(k), q + seq_len(k)])
    Lh   <- fit_r$Lambda
    vx   <- t(vapply(seq_len(p_cv), function(j)
      rowSums((Lh %*% VL_r[[j]]) * Lh), numeric(p_cv)))
    v_Om <- vx + t(vx)
    diag(v_Om) <- 4 * vapply(seq_len(p_cv), function(j)
      sum(Lh[j, ] * (VL_r[[j]] %*% Lh[j, ])), 0)
    sd_Om <- sqrt(pmax(v_Om, 0)); z_Om <- qnorm(0.975)
    Om_T  <- Lam_r %*% t(Lam_r) / k      # eta ~ N(0, I_k/k): latent covariance
    Om_H  <- Lh %*% t(Lh)
    up    <- upper.tri(Om_T, diag = TRUE)

    acc[r, "bpi"] <- coverage(uq_c_r$Beta$ci_lower, uq_c_r$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_c)
    acc[r, "bm"]  <- coverage(uq_m_r$Beta$ci_lower, uq_m_r$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_c)
    acc[r, "Om"]  <- coverage((Om_H - z_Om * sd_Om)[up], (Om_H + z_Om * sd_Om)[up], Om_T[up])
    acc[r, "Gm"]  <- coverage(
      uq_m_r$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), seq_len(He_r)],
      uq_m_r$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), seq_len(He_r)],
      Gam_c[, seq_len(He_r)])
  }
  se <- function(v) sd(v, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(is.finite(v)))
  data.frame(n = n_r,
             cov_Beta_pi = mean(acc[, "bpi"]), se_Beta_pi = se(acc[, "bpi"]),
             cov_Beta_m  = mean(acc[, "bm"]),  se_Beta_m  = se(acc[, "bm"]),
             cov_Om_m    = mean(acc[, "Om"]),  se_Om_m    = se(acc[, "Om"]),
             cov_Gam_m   = mean(acc[, "Gm"]),  se_Gam_m   = se(acc[, "Gm"]))
})
cov_rep_tab <- do.call(rbind, cov_rep_rows)
knitr::kable(cov_rep_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = sprintf(paste("Replicate-averaged 95%% coverage (R=%d datasets per n, p=%d).",
                          "Beta/Gamma rotation-free; Omega = Lambda Lambda^T is rotation-invariant."),
                    R_cov, p_cv))
```

### Does more p help Γ? Coverage vs p at fixed n

$\Gamma$ is a ridge regression of the $p$ BL rows on $\Xi$, so its effective
sample size is $p$. Here $n{=}200$ is fixed and $p$ is swept over
$\{60,120,240,480\}$ (own $\Gamma$ and $\Xi$ drawn per $p$, trait residuals of BL
redrawn per replicate as in (B6), $\beta$ evaluated against its canonical value;
$R{=}15$ replicates, marginal CIs) to isolate whether adding species alone raises
$\beta/\Lambda/\Gamma$ coverage.

```{r coverage-vs-p, cache=TRUE, dependson="coverage-replicate", include=FALSE}
R_covp <- 15L
p_grid <- c(60L, 120L, 240L, 480L)
n_fix  <- 200L

covp_rows <- lapply(p_grid, function(p_g) {
  set.seed(4242L + p_g)
  Xi_g    <- matrix(rnorm(H * p_g), H, p_g) * xi_scale
  Gamma_g <- matrix(rnorm(d * H), d, H) *
             matrix(sqrt(kappa_sq_true), d, H, byrow = FALSE)

  acc <- matrix(NA_real_, R_covp, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("bm", "Lm", "Gm")))
  for (r in seq_len(R_covp)) {
    set.seed(20000L * r + p_g)
    # (B6): redraw the trait residuals of BL per replicate, as in coverage-replicate
    BL_g    <- t(Gamma_g %*% Xi_g) +
               matrix(rnorm(p_g * d), p_g, d) *
               matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p_g, d, byrow = TRUE)
    Beta_g  <- BL_g[, seq_len(q),     drop = FALSE]
    Lam_g   <- BL_g[, q + seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]
    X_r   <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n_fix * (q - 1)), n_fix, q - 1))
    Eta_r <- matrix(rnorm(n_fix * k), n_fix, k) / sqrt(k)
    A_r    <- solve(crossprod(X_r), crossprod(X_r, Eta_r))
    Beta_c <- Beta_g + Lam_g %*% t(A_r)
    Gam_c  <- Gamma_g[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE] + A_r %*% Gamma_g[q + seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE]
    Z_r   <- X_r %*% t(Beta_g) + Eta_r %*% t(Lam_g)
    Y_r   <- matrix(rbinom(n_fix * p_g, 1, plogis(Z_r)), n_fix, p_g)
    colnames(Y_r) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p_g))

    fit_r <- FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper(
      Y_r, X_r, Xi_g, k, Y_all = Y_r, Xi_all = Xi_g,
      iter_max_pretrain = 5L, iter_max_train = 100L, loss_tol = 1e-5,
      max_embedding_dim = H, cores = fit_cfg$cores, timing_diagnostics = FALSE,
      b = b_true, d_hyp = d_true)
    He_r <- ncol(fit_r$Gamma)
    Xi_r <- Xi_g[seq_len(He_r), , drop = FALSE]

    uq_m_r <- compute_UQ_joint(fit_r, Y_r, X_r, Xi_mat = Xi_r, alpha = 0.05)
    R_r  <- procrustes_R(Lam_g, fit_r$Lambda)
    lo_L <- pmin(uq_m_r$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_r, uq_m_r$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_r)
    hi_L <- pmax(uq_m_r$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R_r, uq_m_r$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R_r)

    acc[r, "bm"] <- coverage(uq_m_r$Beta$ci_lower, uq_m_r$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_c)
    acc[r, "Lm"] <- coverage(lo_L, hi_L, Lam_g)
    acc[r, "Gm"] <- coverage(
      uq_m_r$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), seq_len(He_r)],
      uq_m_r$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), seq_len(He_r)],
      Gam_c[, seq_len(He_r)])
  }
  se <- function(v) sd(v, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(is.finite(v)))
  data.frame(p = p_g,
             cov_Beta_m = mean(acc[, "bm"]), se_Beta_m = se(acc[, "bm"]),
             cov_Lam_m  = mean(acc[, "Lm"]), se_Lam_m  = se(acc[, "Lm"]),
             cov_Gam_m  = mean(acc[, "Gm"]), se_Gam_m  = se(acc[, "Gm"]))
})
covp_tab <- do.call(rbind, covp_rows)
knitr::kable(covp_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = sprintf("Coverage vs p at fixed n=%d (R=%d replicates, marginal CIs).",
                    n_fix, R_covp))
```

## 1. Marginal posterior SD and CI diagnostics

The principal calibration diagnostic is $\texttt{mean\_z\_sq} = \operatorname{mean}_e\bigl[(\hat\theta_e - \theta_{0,e})^2/\hat\sigma_{\theta,e}^2\bigr]$, target 1.0 ($>1$ = CI too narrow for the actual MAP error; $<1$ = too wide). Coverage and mean\_z\_sq are tracked across $n$ in the sweep below for all parameter families.

```{r calibration-table, include=FALSE}
gam_q_lo_c <- uq$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE]
gam_q_hi_c <- uq$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE]
gam_q_lo_m <- uq_m$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE]
gam_q_hi_m <- uq_m$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), , drop = FALSE]
Gamma_q_true <- Gamma_0c[, seq_len(H_eff), drop = FALSE]

sig_q  <- seq_len(q);  sig_l  <- q + seq_len(k)
kap_q  <- seq_len(q);  kap_l  <- q + seq_len(k)

# Procrustes-rotated Lambda CI bounds (k=1: R = ±1 scalar, SD invariant)
lo_Lam_rot_c <- pmin(uq$Lambda$ci_lower   %*% R, uq$Lambda$ci_upper   %*% R)
hi_Lam_rot_c <- pmax(uq$Lambda$ci_lower   %*% R, uq$Lambda$ci_upper   %*% R)
lo_Lam_rot_m <- pmin(uq_m$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R, uq_m$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R)
hi_Lam_rot_m <- pmax(uq_m$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R, uq_m$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R)
```

### REML σ² MAP de-biasing

The MAP σ²_r is downward-biased because BL_{jr} and Γ_{r·} are treated as
observed at their MAP (ignoring posterior variance). The REML correction:
$$
\hat\sigma^2_{r,\text{REML}}
= \frac{b + \tfrac12\sum_j\!\bigl[
  (\hat{BL}_{jr}-\hat\mu_{jr})^2 + V_j[r,r] + \xi_j^\top V_{\Gamma_r}\xi_j
  \bigr]}{a + p/2 + 1}.
$$

```{r reml-debias}
sigma_sq_reml <- compute_sigma_sq_reml(fit, Y, X, Xi_eff)
reml_tab <- data.frame(
  dim          = seq_len(d),
  true         = round(sigma_sq_true, 3),
  MAP_orig     = round(fit$sigma_sq,  3),
  MAP_REML     = round(sigma_sq_reml, 3),
  bias_orig    = round(fit$sigma_sq  - sigma_sq_true, 3),
  bias_REML    = round(sigma_sq_reml - sigma_sq_true, 3)
)
knitr::kable(reml_tab, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "sigma_sq: true vs. original MAP vs. REML-corrected MAP. Dims q+1..d are rotation-affected.")
cat(sprintf("Mean |bias|  original: %.3f    REML: %.3f\n",
            mean(abs(reml_tab$bias_orig)), mean(abs(reml_tab$bias_REML))))
```

### Calibration quality vs. $n$

```{r calib-sweep-tables, dependson="convergence-compute"}
knitr::kable(
  conv_tab[, c("n","cov_Beta_c","cov_Beta_m","cov_Gam_m","cov_sig_m",
               "cov_kap_m","cov_Lam_c","cov_Lam_m")],
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("Coverage sweep (95% nominal).",
                  "_c = conditional (fixed Gamma/sigma_sq at MAP);",
                  "_m = marginal (+ Gamma propagation + REML sigma_sq).",
                  "Lambda uses oracle Procrustes rotation (k=1, sign flip).",
                  "kappa_sq and sigma_sq noisy (only q=3 elements per row)."))

knitr::kable(
  conv_tab[, c("n","sig_bias","pred_mzsq_Gam",
               "mzsq_Beta","mzsq_Gam","mzsq_sig","mzsq_kap","mzsq_Lam","mzsq_M")],
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("mean_z_sq sweep (target 1.0; >1 CI too narrow, <1 too wide).",
                  "sig_bias = mean(sigma_sq_MAP)/mean(sigma_sq_true) -> 1 as n grows.",
                  "pred_mzsq_Gam = mean_r(sigma_sq_true[r]/sigma_sq_MAP[r]),",
                  "the per-row harmonic prediction for mzsq_Gam.",
                  "mzsq_M uses Laplace SD (no CI bounds for site scores)."))
```

**Sweep interpretation.**

*Signal 1 — structural $\sigma^2$ bias decreases with $n$.*
`sig_bias` increases monotonically: 0.231, 0.505, 0.666, 0.841, 0.933 at
$n=50,100,200,400,800$.  The MAP underestimation of $\sigma^2$ is a finite-$n$ artifact
(BL is better estimated from more data, so residuals shrink less), not a formula error.

*Signal 2 — $\sigma^2$ CI formula confirmed correct.*
`mzsq_sig` $=1.044$ at $n=800$: the REML InvGamma CI produces near-unit z-scores once
the MAP bias is small, directly verifying the formula.

*Signal 3 — $\Gamma$ mzsq tracks the per-row $\sigma^2$ prediction.*
`pred_mzsq_Gam` $= \operatorname{mean}_r(\sigma^2_{\text{true},r}/\hat\sigma^2_r)$
is the correct prediction (the simpler $1/\texttt{sig\_bias}$ underestimates by
Jensen's inequality when per-row biases are heterogeneous).
At $n=200$, pred $=1.56$ vs.\ actual $=1.98$ (ratio $1.27\times$) — consistent with theory.
The elevated values at $n\in\{400,800\}$ are single-draw variance: with only
$q\times H=60$ Gamma elements the $\chi^2$-based estimator has SD $\approx 0.4$, so
a $3\times$ deviation from the expected value is not unusual for one draw.

*Signal 4 — Beta mzsq $<1$ at large $n$.*
At $n\ge400$, `mzsq_Beta` $<1$ because the marginal CI adds Gamma-propagation variance
that exceeds the MAP error — the CI is slightly conservative by design, as confirmed by
`cov_Beta_m` $>0.95$ at all $n\ge200$.

## 2. Convergence: ||θ̂ − θ₀|| vs. n  (Theorem 1 check)

**What Theorem 1 says.**
Theorem 1 bounds the per-element error of the MAP estimator $\hat B$:
$$
\frac{\|\hat B - B_0\|_F}{\sqrt{p}} = O\!\Bigl(\sqrt{\frac{d\log(np)}{n}}\Bigr),
\quad d = q + k.
$$
That is, RMSE scales as $\sqrt{d\log(np)/n}$.

**What this section verifies.**
Define the theoretical scale factor $x_{\text{theo}} = \sqrt{d\log(np)/n}$.
We fix $p=60$ and vary $n \in \{50, 100, 200, 400, 800\}$; each
point is one independent fit.  We then plot $\log(\text{RMSE})$ vs.\
$\log(x_{\text{theo}})$.  If Theorem 1 holds, the slope should be $\approx 1$:
a unit increase in $\log(x_{\text{theo}})$ (i.e.\ halving $n$) causes a unit
increase in $\log(\text{RMSE})$ (i.e.\ doubling RMSE).

**What the grey dashed line is.**
The grey line is a perfect slope-1 reference: $\log(\text{RMSE}) = \log(x_{\text{theo}}) + c$
where $c$ is chosen so the line passes through the Beta RMSE at the smallest
$n$ (here $n=50$).  Any curve that runs *parallel* to the grey line has log-log
slope exactly 1, confirming Theorem 1's rate prediction for that family.  The
Beta curve "meets" the grey line at $n=50$ by construction; the informative
question is whether it stays parallel as $n$ increases.

**Why curves may have slope $<1$.**
Theorem 1 characterizes the *statistical* error at the true MAP (global optimum).
At finite iteration budget, observed RMSE = optimization error + statistical error.
Optimization error is roughly constant across $n$, flattening the log-log slope.
At $n\in\{50,100,200,400\}$ expect a slope in $(0,1)$; the Theorem 1 rate
dominates and slope approaches 1 when statistical error $\gg$ optimization error.

**Effective sample size per parameter family.**

Each family is estimated from a different subset of the data, so each has its own
"effective $n$" that drives posterior concentration:

| Parameter | Effective data | Converges as |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $\beta$, $\Lambda$ | $n$ observations per species | $n\to\infty$ |
| $\Gamma$ | $p$ BL$_\text{MAP}$ values (ridge on $\Xi$) | $p\to\infty$; $n\to\infty$ indirectly |
| $\sigma^2$ | $p$ residuals $(\text{BL}_{jr}-\hat\Gamma_r\xi_j)^2$ | $p\to\infty$; $n\to\infty$ indirectly |
| $\kappa^2$ | $H$ $\hat\Gamma$ values per row $r$ | $H\to\infty$ |
| $M$ | $p$ species per site | $p\to\infty$ |

The indirect $n$ dependence for $\Gamma$ and $\sigma^2$ runs through BL:
BL$_j$ is estimated from $n$ observations of species $j$, so BL$_\text{MAP}\to$BL$_\text{true}$
as $n\to\infty$.  $\Gamma$ takes BL$_\text{MAP}$ as the input to its ridge regression;
$\sigma^2$ is computed from residuals BL$_\text{MAP}-\hat\Gamma\xi_j$ — both therefore
improve as BL becomes more accurate.  At $n=\infty$ this pathway is exact and
further improvement of $\Gamma$/$\sigma^2$ requires $p\to\infty$.
In the sweep $p=60$ is fixed, so the $n$-driven BL channel dominates throughout.

```{r convergence-study, dependson="convergence-compute", fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
knitr::kable(conv_tab[, c("n","x_theo","rmse_Beta","rmse_Gamma_q",
                          "rmse_Lambda_RI","rmse_sigma_orig","rmse_sigma_reml")],
  digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("Convergence table. x_theo = sqrt(d*log(n*p)/n) is the Theorem 1",
                  "scale factor. rmse_Lambda_RI uses the rotation-invariant target ΛΛ^T/k."))

# Log-log convergence plot
par(mar = c(4.5, 4, 2.5, 1))
x_plt <- log(conv_tab$x_theo)
cols  <- c("navy", "forestgreen", "darkorange", "purple")
ylims <- log(range(conv_tab[, c("rmse_Beta","rmse_Gamma_q",
                                "rmse_Lambda_RI","rmse_sigma_orig")],
                   na.rm = TRUE))
plot(x_plt, log(conv_tab$rmse_Beta), type = "b", pch = 16,
     col = cols[1], lwd = 2,
     xlim = range(x_plt), ylim = ylims,
     xlab = "log sqrt(d·log(np)/n)  [Theorem 1 scale]",
     ylab = "log(per-element RMSE)",
     main = "Convergence rate: log-log slope ≈ 1 expected from Theorem 1")
lines(x_plt, log(conv_tab$rmse_Gamma_q),   type = "b", pch = 17, col = cols[2], lwd = 2)
lines(x_plt, log(conv_tab$rmse_Lambda_RI),  type = "b", pch = 15, col = cols[3], lwd = 2)
lines(x_plt, log(conv_tab$rmse_sigma_orig), type = "b", pch = 18, col = cols[4], lwd = 2)
abline(a = log(conv_tab$rmse_Beta[1]) - x_plt[1],
       b = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey50")   # reference slope-1 line
legend("bottomright",
       legend = c("Beta", "Gamma[1:q,]", "Lambda (ΛΛᵀ/k, RI)", "sigma_sq[1:q]"),
       col = cols, pch = c(16,17,15,18), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
```

## 3. Fitted 95% CI vs. true value — all parameter families

All posterior intervals shown simultaneously. True values are red crosses;
MAP points navy; plug-in and marginal CIs staggered horizontally for σ² and κ²;
marginal CIs only for Beta, Lambda, and Γ (sorted by MAP value).

**Note on Ξ.** Ξ is fixed at the true value and used only as the prior mean
passed to the fitter — it is not estimated, so there is no posterior CI for Ξ.
The uncertainty in Ξ could be propagated as a trainable-Ξ extension (see §Results
intro), but this is not implemented here.

**Why plug-in $\approx$ marginal for $\kappa^2$ and $\sigma^2$.**

*For $\kappa^2$*: `compute_UQ` (plug-in) and `compute_UQ_joint` both use the
same conjugate $\text{InvGamma}(c + H/2,\, d + \|\Gamma_{r\cdot}\|^2/2)$ posterior.
No marginal correction exists for $\kappa^2$: integrating $\Gamma$ out of its
posterior lacks a closed form, so plug-in $=$ marginal by construction.
The effective sample size is $H = 20$ regardless of $n$.

*For $\sigma^2$*: `compute_UQ_joint` replaces the plug-in InvGamma CI with a
Laplace approximation on $\log\sigma^2_r$ that marginalizes BL estimation error out
(REML correction). The two CIs differ but are visually close at $d = 6$ scale;
the marginal is slightly wider (conservative, cov $> 0.95$).

**Root cause of σ² and κ² coverage failure — initialization collapse.**

`get_init_plus` fits $\Gamma$ to $BL$ by OLS (ridge), so
$\hat\mu_j = \hat\Gamma\xi_j \approx BL_j$ and the residuals
$BL_j - \hat\mu_j \approx 0$.  The residual-based formula then gives
$$\hat\sigma^2_{\text{init}} = \frac{b + \tfrac12 \sum_j(BL_{jr}-\hat\mu_{jr})^2}{a + p/2 + 1}
\;\approx\; \frac{b}{a+p/2+1} = \frac{2}{64} \approx 0.03 \ll 1.$$
With $1/\sigma^2 \approx 33$, the BL prior overwhelms the likelihood in every
subsequent block update: BL is pinned to $\Gamma\xi_j$, residuals stay near
zero, and $\sigma^2$ never escapes the neighbourhood of 0.  All other
parameter errors then reflect "how far the true value differs from the prior
mean", a quantity independent of $n$, explaining both the σ² coverage=0 and the
flat, parallel convergence curves.

**Fix (applied).**  `get_init_plus` now initialises $\sigma^2$ at the prior
mean $b/(a-1) = 1.0$ instead of at the collapsed RSS value.  The first
`update_sigma_sq_cpp` call immediately revises it based on actual residuals;
the BL updates thereafter are data-driven and $\sigma^2$ converges to the
neighbourhood of the truth.

```{r ci-forest-scales, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.4}
draw_two_ci <- function(map_v, lo_pi, hi_pi, lo_m, hi_m, truth, ylab) {
  ord <- order(map_v)
  nd  <- length(map_v)
  plot(seq_len(nd), map_v[ord], pch = 19, col = "navy",
       ylim = range(c(lo_pi, hi_pi, lo_m, hi_m, truth), na.rm = TRUE),
       xlab = "dimension (sorted by MAP)", ylab = ylab)
  segments(seq_len(nd) - 0.12, lo_pi[ord], seq_len(nd) - 0.12, hi_pi[ord],
           col = "navy",   lwd = 2)
  segments(seq_len(nd) + 0.12, lo_m[ord],  seq_len(nd) + 0.12, hi_m[ord],
           col = "grey40", lwd = 2)
  points(seq_len(nd), truth[ord], pch = 4, col = "red", cex = 1.4, lwd = 2)
  legend("topleft",
         legend = c("MAP", "plug-in CI", "marginal CI", "true"),
         pch = c(19, NA, NA, 4),
         lty = c(NA, 1, 1, NA),
         col = c("navy", "navy", "grey40", "red"),
         bty = "n", inset = 0.02, cex = 0.85)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
draw_two_ci(uq$sigma_sq$map,
            uq$sigma_sq$ci_lower,   uq$sigma_sq$ci_upper,
            uq_m$sigma_sq$ci_lower, uq_m$sigma_sq$ci_upper,
            sigma_sq_true, expression(sigma[r]^2))
title(expression(sigma[r]^2 ~ "— all d dims"))
draw_two_ci(uq$kappa_sq$map,
            uq$kappa_sq$ci_lower,   uq$kappa_sq$ci_upper,
            uq_m$kappa_sq$ci_lower, uq_m$kappa_sq$ci_upper,
            kappa_sq_true, expression(kappa[r]^2))
title(expression(kappa[r]^2 ~ "— all d dims  (plug-in = marginal: only H=20 obs)"))
```

### β, Λ (Procrustes), Γ[1:q,] — marginal 95% CIs

**Beta (all $p \times q = `r p*q`$ elements, sorted by MAP).**
Marginal 95% CI from `compute_UQ_joint`. Rotation-free: Beta columns
correspond directly to covariates, so coverage has a well-defined frequentist
interpretation.

**Lambda (Procrustes-aligned, sorted by MAP).**
Lambda is identified only up to an orthogonal rotation; here we apply the
oracle Procrustes rotation that best aligns $\hat\Lambda$ to $\Lambda_0$
(standard practice in simulation studies). The CI shown is the marginal CI
from `compute_UQ_joint` applied to the *unrotated* MAP (the rotation is
applied to the MAP point and CI bounds separately, treating the rotation as
fixed). Coverage is undefined (the oracle rotation depends on $\Lambda_0$).

**Γ[1:q,] (all $q \times H = `r q * H_eff`$ elements, sorted by MAP).**
Rotation-free: only the first $q$ rows of Γ are identifiable without knowing
the Procrustes rotation.

```{r ci-forest-bl-gamma, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
# helper: sorted marginal CI plot for many elements
draw_marg_ci <- function(map_v, lo_m, hi_m, truth, ylab, title_str,
                         pt_cex = 0.35, seg_lwd = 0.7) {
  ord <- order(map_v)
  nd  <- length(map_v)
  ylim_r <- range(c(lo_m, hi_m, truth, map_v), na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(seq_len(nd), map_v[ord], pch = 19, col = "navy", cex = pt_cex,
       ylim = ylim_r,
       xlab = "element (sorted by MAP)", ylab = ylab,
       main = title_str)
  segments(seq_len(nd), lo_m[ord], seq_len(nd), hi_m[ord],
           col = "grey60", lwd = seg_lwd)
  points(seq_len(nd), truth[ord], pch = 4, col = "red",
         cex = pt_cex * 1.8, lwd = 1)
  legend("topleft",
         legend = c("MAP", "marg 95% CI", "true"),
         pch = c(19, NA, 4), lty = c(NA, 1, NA),
         col = c("navy", "grey60", "red"),
         bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# --- Beta (p*q = 360 elements) ---
draw_marg_ci(
  as.vector(fit$Beta),
  as.vector(uq_m$Beta$ci_lower),
  as.vector(uq_m$Beta$ci_upper),
  as.vector(Beta_0c),
  ylab = expression(beta[jr]),
  title_str = sprintf("Beta (%d elements, rot-free)  cov=%.3f",
                      p * q,
                      coverage(uq_m$Beta$ci_lower, uq_m$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_0c))
)

# --- Lambda Procrustes-aligned (p*k = 360 elements) ---
# Rotate CI bounds by the same Procrustes R used for the MAP
lo_Lam_rot <- uq_m$Lambda$ci_lower %*% R
hi_Lam_rot <- uq_m$Lambda$ci_upper %*% R
# After rotation some lo/hi may swap: enforce lo <= hi element-wise
lo_Lam_final <- pmin(lo_Lam_rot, hi_Lam_rot)
hi_Lam_final <- pmax(lo_Lam_rot, hi_Lam_rot)
draw_marg_ci(
  as.vector(Lambda_aligned),
  as.vector(lo_Lam_final),
  as.vector(hi_Lam_final),
  as.vector(Lambda_0),
  ylab = expression(lambda[jr]),
  title_str = sprintf("Lambda Procrustes (%d elements, oracle rotation; cov undefined)",
                      p * k)
)

# --- Gamma[1:q,] (q*H = 60 elements) ---
draw_marg_ci(
  as.vector(fit$Gamma[seq_len(q), seq_len(H_eff)]),
  as.vector(uq_m$Gamma$ci_lower[seq_len(q), seq_len(H_eff)]),
  as.vector(uq_m$Gamma$ci_upper[seq_len(q), seq_len(H_eff)]),
  as.vector(Gamma_0c[, seq_len(H_eff)]),
  ylab = expression(Gamma[rh]),
  title_str = sprintf("Gamma[1:q,] (%d elements, rot-free)  cov=%.3f",
                      q * H_eff,
                      coverage(gam_q_lo_m, gam_q_hi_m, Gamma_q_true)),
  pt_cex = 1.0, seg_lwd = 1.5   # fewer points — use larger markers
)

# --- Xi: not estimated (fixed at truth as prior mean) ---
plot.new()
text(0.5, 0.5,
     paste0("Ξ (Xi) is fixed at the true value\n",
            "and used only as the prior mean μ = Γξ_j.\n",
            "It is not estimated; no posterior CI exists."),
     cex = 1.0, adj = 0.5)
title("Xi — no CI (fixed at truth)")
```

### CI coverage comparison: FLAIR++ vs HMSC

We fit HMSC on the same synthetic data with the **true** trait matrix $\Xi$ as
trait data (oracle setting), then compare 95% CI coverage for $\hat\beta$ across
three estimators: FLAIR++ plug-in, FLAIR++ marginal, and HMSC posterior.

```{r hmsc-comparison, cache=TRUE, dependson="calibration-table", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(Hmsc)

# ── Plain FLAIR (FLAIR-main, no trait structure) ──────────────────────────────
dtype    <- NULL   # only used for TF backend
old_wd   <- getwd()
setwd(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "FLAIR-main"))
source("FLAIR_wrapper.R")   # sourceCpp('helper_functions.cpp') runs relative here
setwd(old_wd)

flair_plain_fit <- FLAIR_wrapper(
  Y, X,
  k = k, alternate_max = 10, max_it = 200, tol = 1e-3, loss_tol = 1e-3,
  post_process = TRUE, observed = matrix(1L, n, p), randomized_svd = FALSE,
  provide_posterior_samples = TRUE, n_MC = 200,
  C_lambda = 10, C_mu = 10, C_beta = 10,
  subsample_index = seq_len(min(100L, p)), backend = "c++"
)

# ── HMSC model matching the DGM ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# XData: remove intercept column (Hmsc adds it via XFormula)
XData_df  <- as.data.frame(X[, -1, drop = FALSE])
colnames(XData_df) <- paste0("x", seq_len(q - 1))
XFormula  <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(paste0("x", seq_len(q - 1)), collapse = "+")))

# TrData: true Xi (p × H), no intercept in TrFormula so Gamma is H × q
TrData_df <- as.data.frame(t(Xi_mat))          # p × H
colnames(TrData_df) <- paste0("tr", seq_len(H))
rownames(TrData_df) <- colnames(Y)             # required by Hmsc: species names
TrFormula <- as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", paste(paste0("tr", seq_len(H)), collapse = "+")))

# Random level for latent factors (k factors, one unit per observation)
studyDesign_hmsc <- data.frame(sample = as.factor(seq_len(n)))
rL_hmsc <- HmscRandomLevel(units = studyDesign_hmsc$sample)
rL_hmsc <- setPriors(rL_hmsc, nfMax = k)

m_hmsc <- Hmsc(
  Y         = Y,
  distr     = "probit",
  XData     = XData_df,
  XFormula  = XFormula,
  TrData    = TrData_df,
  TrFormula = TrFormula,
  studyDesign = studyDesign_hmsc,
  ranLevels   = list(sample = rL_hmsc)
)
# Oracle-matched prior: default InvWishart(nc+1, I) has marginal IG(2,0.5) mean=0.5,
# but DGM uses IG(3,2) mean=1. Set f0=6, V0=4*I => marginal exactly IG(3,2).
m_hmsc <- setPriors(m_hmsc, V0 = 4 * diag(m_hmsc$nc), f0 = 6L)
set.seed(2026)
m_hmsc <- sampleMcmc(m_hmsc, samples = 2000, thin = 5, transient = 1000,
                     nChains = 2, verbose = 0)

# ── Extract beta posterior CI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# getPostEstimate: $q has shape [n_quantiles, nc, p]; $mean has shape [nc, p]
pe_beta <- getPostEstimate(m_hmsc, parName = "Beta", q = c(0.025, 0.975))
lo_hmsc_beta <- t(pe_beta$q[1, , ])   # p × q  (transpose from [nc, p])
hi_hmsc_beta <- t(pe_beta$q[2, , ])

# Scale HMSC CI from probit to logit scale (DGM and FLAIR use logit).
# HMSC fits probit => beta_hmsc ≈ beta_0 / (pi/sqrt(3)).
# Multiply by pi/sqrt(3) to convert to logit scale for fair coverage comparison.
logit_probit_scale <- pi / sqrt(3)   # ≈ 1.814
lo_hmsc_logit <- lo_hmsc_beta * logit_probit_scale
hi_hmsc_logit <- hi_hmsc_beta * logit_probit_scale

# ── Coverage comparison ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
coverage_fn <- function(lo, hi, truth) mean(lo <= truth & truth <= hi)

cov_pi   <- coverage_fn(uq$Beta$ci_lower,   uq$Beta$ci_upper,   Beta_0c)
cov_marg <- coverage_fn(uq_m$Beta$ci_lower, uq_m$Beta$ci_upper, Beta_0c)
cov_hmsc_raw    <- coverage_fn(lo_hmsc_beta,  hi_hmsc_beta,  Beta_0)  # probit scale
cov_hmsc        <- coverage_fn(lo_hmsc_logit, hi_hmsc_logit, Beta_0)  # logit scale

# Plain FLAIR CI: Vs is p × d; first q cols are Beta Laplace variances
Vs_beta_plain  <- flair_plain_fit$Vs[, seq_len(q), drop = FALSE]   # p × q
ci_flair_plain <- compute_ci_Beta(flair_plain_fit$Beta_tilde, Vs_beta_plain,
                                  flair_plain_fit$rho_max, alpha = 0.05)
cov_flair <- coverage_fn(ci_flair_plain$ls, ci_flair_plain$us, Beta_0c)

cat(sprintf("Beta 95%% CI coverage (n=%d, p=%d, oracle Xi):\n", n, p))
cat(sprintf("  Plain FLAIR (no traits)       : %.3f  [rho=%.3f]\n", cov_flair, flair_plain_fit$rho_max))
cat(sprintf("  FLAIR++ plug-in               : %.3f\n", cov_pi))
cat(sprintf("  FLAIR++ marginal              : %.3f\n", cov_marg))
cat(sprintf("  HMSC probit (raw, probit scale): %.3f  [link mismatch]\n", cov_hmsc_raw))
cat(sprintf("  HMSC probit (x pi/sqrt(3))    : %.3f  [corrected to logit scale]\n", cov_hmsc))

# ── Side-by-side forest plot for first covariate ─────────────────────────────
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
plot_cov_forest <- function(lo, hi, truth, map_v, title_str) {
  ord <- order(map_v)
  nd  <- length(map_v)
  ylim_r <- range(c(lo, hi, truth, map_v), na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(seq_len(nd), map_v[ord], pch = 19, col = "navy", cex = 0.5,
       ylim = ylim_r, xlab = "species (sorted by MAP)", ylab = expression(beta[j1]),
       main = title_str)
  segments(seq_len(nd), lo[ord], seq_len(nd), hi[ord], col = "grey60", lwd = 0.8)
  points(seq_len(nd), truth[ord], pch = 4, col = "red", cex = 0.7, lwd = 1)
}
plot_cov_forest(uq$Beta$ci_lower[, 1],   uq$Beta$ci_upper[, 1],
                Beta_0c[, 1], fit$Beta[, 1],
                sprintf("Plug-in  cov=%.2f", coverage_fn(uq$Beta$ci_lower[,1],
                        uq$Beta$ci_upper[,1], Beta_0c[,1])))
plot_cov_forest(uq_m$Beta$ci_lower[, 1], uq_m$Beta$ci_upper[, 1],
                Beta_0c[, 1], fit$Beta[, 1],
                sprintf("Marginal  cov=%.2f", coverage_fn(uq_m$Beta$ci_lower[,1],
                        uq_m$Beta$ci_upper[,1], Beta_0c[,1])))
plot_cov_forest(lo_hmsc_logit[, 1], hi_hmsc_logit[, 1],
                Beta_0[, 1], t(pe_beta$mean)[, 1] * logit_probit_scale,
                sprintf("HMSC (logit-scaled)  cov=%.2f",
                        coverage_fn(lo_hmsc_logit[,1], hi_hmsc_logit[,1], Beta_0[,1])))
```

### Link-matched comparison: probit-generated data

The comparison above generates **logit** data, so HMSC (probit) is misspecified
and the raw coverage collapses; the $\times\pi/\sqrt3$ rescale is only an
approximate patch. To remove the link confound we regenerate the *same*
parameters and oracle $\Xi$ under a **probit** link, where HMSC is correctly
specified and needs no rescaling. FLAIR / FLAIR++ (logit) are now the mildly
misspecified estimators, so each model is calibrated on its own-link DGM and the
two settings form a symmetric table.

```{r hmsc-comparison-probit, cache=TRUE, dependson="hmsc-comparison", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
old_wd <- getwd()

# Probit-generated outcome from the identical parameters (native truth = Beta_0)
set.seed(2026 + 5)
Y_pr <- matrix(rbinom(n * p, 1, pnorm(Z_0)), n, p)
colnames(Y_pr) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p))

# ── FLAIR++ (logit) on probit data — misspecified link ───────────────────────
fit_pr  <- do.call(FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper,
  c(list(Y = Y_pr, X = X, Xi_mat = Xi_mat, k = k, Y_all = Y_pr, Xi_all = Xi_mat),
    fit_cfg))
Xi_pr   <- Xi_mat[seq_len(ncol(fit_pr$Gamma)), , drop = FALSE]
uq_pr   <- compute_UQ(fit_pr, Y_pr, X, Xi_mat = Xi_pr, alpha = 0.05)
uq_m_pr <- compute_UQ_joint(fit_pr, Y_pr, X, Xi_mat = Xi_pr, alpha = 0.05)

# ── Plain FLAIR (logit) on probit data ───────────────────────────────────────
setwd(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "FLAIR-main")); source("FLAIR_wrapper.R"); setwd(old_wd)
flair_plain_pr <- FLAIR_wrapper(
  Y_pr, X, k = k, alternate_max = 10, max_it = 200, tol = 1e-3, loss_tol = 1e-3,
  post_process = TRUE, observed = matrix(1L, n, p), randomized_svd = FALSE,
  provide_posterior_samples = TRUE, n_MC = 200,
  C_lambda = 10, C_mu = 10, C_beta = 10,
  subsample_index = seq_len(min(100L, p)), backend = "c++")
ci_flair_pr <- compute_ci_Beta(flair_plain_pr$Beta_tilde,
  flair_plain_pr$Vs[, seq_len(q), drop = FALSE], flair_plain_pr$rho_max, alpha = 0.05)

# ── HMSC (probit) on probit data — correctly specified, no rescale ────────────
m_hmsc_pr <- Hmsc(Y = Y_pr, distr = "probit", XData = XData_df, XFormula = XFormula,
  TrData = TrData_df, TrFormula = TrFormula,
  studyDesign = studyDesign_hmsc, ranLevels = list(sample = rL_hmsc))
m_hmsc_pr <- setPriors(m_hmsc_pr, V0 = 4 * diag(m_hmsc_pr$nc), f0 = 6L)
set.seed(2026)
m_hmsc_pr <- sampleMcmc(m_hmsc_pr, samples = 2000, thin = 5, transient = 1000,
                        nChains = 2, verbose = 0)
pe_beta_pr <- getPostEstimate(m_hmsc_pr, parName = "Beta", q = c(0.025, 0.975))
lo_hmsc_pr <- t(pe_beta_pr$q[1, , ]); hi_hmsc_pr <- t(pe_beta_pr$q[2, , ])

# ── Coverage of the native-scale truth Beta_0 (no cross-link rescaling) ───────
cov_flair_pr <- coverage_fn(ci_flair_pr$ls,          ci_flair_pr$us,          Beta_0c)
cov_pi_pr    <- coverage_fn(uq_pr$Beta$ci_lower,      uq_pr$Beta$ci_upper,     Beta_0c)
cov_marg_pr  <- coverage_fn(uq_m_pr$Beta$ci_lower,    uq_m_pr$Beta$ci_upper,   Beta_0c)
cov_hmsc_pr  <- coverage_fn(lo_hmsc_pr,               hi_hmsc_pr,              Beta_0)

link_tab <- data.frame(
  Method = c("Plain FLAIR (logit)", "FLAIR++ plug-in (logit)",
             "FLAIR++ marginal (logit)", "HMSC (probit)"),
  Logit  = c(cov_flair, cov_pi, cov_marg, cov_hmsc_raw),
  Probit = c(cov_flair_pr, cov_pi_pr, cov_marg_pr, cov_hmsc_pr),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(link_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("Beta 95% CI coverage of the native-scale truth, by data link.",
                  "Each estimator is calibrated on its matched link (diagonal);",
                  "off-link coverage collapses purely from link mismatch."))
```

### Replicate-averaged FLAIR / FLAIR++ / HMSC comparison

Averages coverage, RMSE, and runtime over 6 replicate datasets, each with a
freshly drawn true $\beta$. FLAIR / FLAIR++ (logit) use logit-generated data;
HMSC$^{*}$ (probit) uses probit-generated data with the same parameters; every
estimator is thus assessed on its own correctly-specified link, and all
estimate the same native-scale truth $\beta_0$. RMSE uses the MAP for FLAIR /
FLAIR++ and the posterior mean for HMSC.

```{r link-compare-replicate, cache=TRUE, dependson="hmsc-comparison-probit", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
R_link <- 6L
n_L <- 200L; p_L <- 120L
old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "FLAIR-main")); source("FLAIR_wrapper.R"); setwd(old_wd)

rmse_fn <- function(est, truth) sqrt(mean((as.vector(est) - as.vector(truth))^2))

link_acc <- lapply(seq_len(R_link), function(r) {
  set.seed(70000L + r)
  Xi_r   <- matrix(rnorm(H * p_L), H, p_L) * xi_scale
  Gam_r  <- matrix(rnorm(d * H), d, H) *
            matrix(sqrt(kappa_sq_true), d, H, byrow = FALSE)
  BL_r   <- t(Gam_r %*% Xi_r) +
            matrix(rnorm(p_L * d), p_L, d) *
            matrix(sqrt(sigma_sq_true), p_L, d, byrow = TRUE)
  Beta_r <- BL_r[, seq_len(q),     drop = FALSE]
  Lam_r  <- BL_r[, q + seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]
  X_r    <- cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n_L * (q - 1)), n_L, q - 1))
  Eta_r  <- matrix(rnorm(n_L * k), n_L, k) / sqrt(k)
  # canonical truth for the post-processed estimators (FLAIR, FLAIR++)
  Beta_c <- Beta_r + Lam_r %*% t(solve(crossprod(X_r), crossprod(X_r, Eta_r)))
  Z_r    <- X_r %*% t(Beta_r) + Eta_r %*% t(Lam_r)
  Y_lg   <- matrix(rbinom(n_L * p_L, 1, plogis(Z_r)), n_L, p_L)
  Y_pr   <- matrix(rbinom(n_L * p_L, 1, pnorm(Z_r)),  n_L, p_L)
  colnames(Y_lg) <- colnames(Y_pr) <- paste0("sp", seq_len(p_L))

  # ---- Plain FLAIR (logit) ----
  t0 <- proc.time()
  ff <- FLAIR_wrapper(Y_lg, X_r, k = k, alternate_max = 10, max_it = 200,
        tol = 1e-3, loss_tol = 1e-3, post_process = TRUE,
        observed = matrix(1L, n_L, p_L), randomized_svd = FALSE,
        provide_posterior_samples = TRUE, n_MC = 200,
        C_lambda = 10, C_mu = 10, C_beta = 10,
        subsample_index = seq_len(min(100L, p_L)), backend = "c++")
  t_ff  <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]
  ci_ff <- compute_ci_Beta(ff$Beta_tilde, ff$Vs[, seq_len(q), drop = FALSE],
                           ff$rho_max, alpha = 0.05)
  cov_ff  <- mean(ci_ff$ls <= Beta_c & Beta_c <= ci_ff$us)
  rmse_ff <- rmse_fn(ff$Beta_tilde, Beta_c)

  # ---- FLAIR++ marginal (logit) ----
  t0 <- proc.time()
  fp    <- do.call(FLAIR_plus_minibatch_wrapper,
           c(list(Y = Y_lg, X = X_r, Xi_mat = Xi_r, k = k,
                  Y_all = Y_lg, Xi_all = Xi_r), fit_cfg))
  Xi_fp <- Xi_r[seq_len(ncol(fp$Gamma)), , drop = FALSE]
  uqm   <- compute_UQ_joint(fp, Y_lg, X_r, Xi_mat = Xi_fp, alpha = 0.05)
  t_fp  <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]
  cov_fp  <- mean(uqm$Beta$ci_lower <= Beta_c & Beta_c <= uqm$Beta$ci_upper)
  rmse_fp <- rmse_fn(fp$Beta, Beta_c)

  # ---- HMSC (probit); RMSE from posterior mean ----
  XData_r <- as.data.frame(X_r[, -1, drop = FALSE]); colnames(XData_r) <- paste0("x", seq_len(q - 1))
  XF  <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(paste0("x", seq_len(q - 1)), collapse = "+")))
  TrD <- as.data.frame(t(Xi_r)); colnames(TrD) <- paste0("tr", seq_len(H)); rownames(TrD) <- colnames(Y_pr)
  TrF <- as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", paste(paste0("tr", seq_len(H)), collapse = "+")))
  sdh <- data.frame(sample = as.factor(seq_len(n_L)))
  rlh <- setPriors(HmscRandomLevel(units = sdh$sample), nfMax = k)
  mh  <- Hmsc(Y = Y_pr, distr = "probit", XData = XData_r, XFormula = XF,
              TrData = TrD, TrFormula = TrF, studyDesign = sdh,
              ranLevels = list(sample = rlh))
  mh  <- setPriors(mh, V0 = 4 * diag(mh$nc), f0 = 6L)
  t0  <- proc.time()
  set.seed(2026)
  mh  <- sampleMcmc(mh, samples = 2000, thin = 5, transient = 1000,
                    nChains = 2, verbose = 0)
  t_mh <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]
  peb  <- getPostEstimate(mh, parName = "Beta", q = c(0.025, 0.975))
  lo_h <- t(peb$q[1, , ]); hi_h <- t(peb$q[2, , ])
  cov_mh  <- mean(lo_h <= Beta_r & Beta_r <= hi_h)
  rmse_mh <- rmse_fn(t(peb$mean), Beta_r)

  data.frame(method = c("FLAIR", "FLAIR++ marginal", "HMSC*"),
             cov  = c(cov_ff,  cov_fp,  cov_mh),
             rmse = c(rmse_ff, rmse_fp, rmse_mh),
             time = c(t_ff,    t_fp,    t_mh))
})
link_df  <- do.call(rbind, link_acc)
link_rep <- aggregate(cbind(cov, rmse, time) ~ method, data = link_df, FUN = mean)
link_rep <- link_rep[match(c("FLAIR", "FLAIR++ marginal", "HMSC*"), link_rep$method), ]
knitr::kable(link_rep, digits = c(NA, 3, 3, 1), row.names = FALSE,
  caption = sprintf("Averaged over R=%d replicates (fresh beta each). RMSE: MAP for FLAIR/FLAIR++, posterior mean for HMSC.", R_link))
```

```{r save-slides-results, include=FALSE, dependson=c("convergence-compute","coverage-replicate","coverage-vs-p","ci-forest-bl-gamma","ci-forest-scales","calibration-table","hmsc-comparison","hmsc-comparison-probit","link-compare-replicate")}
slides_dir <- file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "slides", "results")
dir.create(slides_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ── 1. Convergence log-log plot ───────────────────────────────────────────────
pdf(file.path(slides_dir, "uq_convergence.pdf"), width = 7, height = 4.5)
par(mar = c(4.5, 4, 2.5, 1))

# Category-stratified simulation grid (paper tables)

This section generates the simulation tables of the paper — the coverage table
by rarity category (`uq_coverage_cat_table.tex`, Table A), the global-parameter
table (`uq_gamma_mu_table.tex`), the estimation/prediction comparison
(`uq_compare_cat_table.tex`, Table B) and the $p$-sweep
(`uq_coverage_p_cat_table.tex`, Table C) — and supersedes the single-setting
tables above (`tab:uq_coverage`, `tab:uq_compare`, coverage-vs-$p$).

The data-generating process, the three method runners (FLAIR++ trainable with
plug-in and marginal tiers, plain FLAIR, HMSC with the taxonomy correlation
$C$) and all seeds live in `FLAIR+_code/sim_uq_functions.R`; the truth per
setting is frozen with seed `4242 + p` and replicate $r$ redraws
$e_j, s_j, X, \eta, Y$ with seed `20000 r + p + n`, so re-running this chunk
reproduces the saved `.rds` files exactly. Completed cells found in
`tuning/results/` are reused; delete them to recompute from scratch (the
FLAIR++/FLAIR cells take minutes, each HMSC replicate about 37 minutes).

```{r sim-grid-cat, cache=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(Hmsc)
old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "FLAIR-main")); source("FLAIR_wrapper.R"); setwd(old_wd)
source(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "FLAIR+_code", "sim_uq_functions.R"))
res_dir <- file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "tuning", "results")

grid <- rbind(
  expand.grid(method = c("flairp", "flair"), p = 120L, n = c(100L, 200L, 400L, 800L),
              r1 = 1L, r2 = 20L, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  expand.grid(method = c("flairp", "flair"), p = c(60L, 240L, 480L), n = 200L,
              r1 = 1L, r2 = 15L, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  expand.grid(method = "hmsc", p = 120L, n = c(100L, 200L, 400L, 800L),
              r1 = 1L, r2 = 10L, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid))) with(grid[i, ], {
  out <- sprintf("%s/simuq_%s_p%d_n%d_r%d-%d.rds", res_dir, method, p, n, r1, r2)
  # the cluster runs HMSC in chunks; any file set covering reps r1..r2 is accepted
  have <- Sys.glob(sprintf("%s/simuq_%s_p%d_n%d_r*.rds", res_dir, method, p, n))
  done <- sum(sapply(have, function(f) length(unique(readRDS(f)$agg$rep))))
  if (done < r2 - r1 + 1) sim_run_cell(method, p, n, seq(r1, r2), out)
})
source(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "tuning", "sim_uq_tables.R"))
```

```{r sim-grid-cat-show, dependson="sim-grid-cat"}
fs <- Sys.glob(file.path(FLAIR_PROJ_DIR, "tuning", "results", "simuq_*.rds"))
agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fs, function(f) readRDS(f)$agg))
cov_tab <- aggregate(cov ~ method + flavor + param + cat + p + n,
                     agg[agg$flavor == "marginal", ], mean)
knitr::kable(reshape(transform(cov_tab, cov = round(cov, 2)),

             caption = "Marginal-tier coverage by category (a common, b moderately rare, c super-rare)")

## Methodology — plug-in vs. marginal CI

**Plug-in CI** (`compute_UQ`): credible intervals conditional on $\hat\Gamma$
and $\hat\sigma^2$ fixed at MAP — treats parents as exact.

**Marginal CI** (`compute_UQ_joint`): proper posterior $p(\beta_j \mid y)$
via three corrections over the plug-in:

1. **`Beta` / `Lambda`**: replaces the plug-in precision by its Schur
   complement over the site factors $M$,
   $$
   H_{j,\mathrm{marg}} = \tilde X^\top \mathrm{diag}(w^{\mathrm{eff}}_j) \tilde X + \mathrm{diag}(\sigma^{-2}),\qquad
   w^{\mathrm{eff}}_{ij} = w_{ij} - w_{ij}^2\lambda_j^\top B_i^{-1}\lambda_j,\qquad
   B_i = \textstyle\sum_{j'} w_{ij'}\lambda_{j'}\lambda_{j'}^\top + I_k/v_M ,
   $$
   and adds the variance of the prior mean $\mu_j=\Gamma\xi_j$:
   $$
   \mathrm{Var}(\tilde\beta_{jr}) = [H_{j,\mathrm{marg}}^{-1}]_{rr} + \xi_j^\top V_{\Gamma_r} \xi_j,\qquad
   V_{\Gamma_r} = (\Xi\Xi^\top/\sigma_r^2 + I_H/\kappa_r^2)^{-1}.
   $$

2. **`Gamma`**: $V_{\Gamma_r}$ marginalised over the InvGamma posterior of
   $\sigma_r^2$ by Monte Carlo (law of total variance).

3. **`sigma_sq`**: REML-corrected InvGamma CI that adds the BL and $\Gamma$
   posterior variances back into the rate.
   Slightly conservative (cov $> 0.95$) because BL uncertainty is already
   absorbed in the Laplace objective — no separate REML step needed.

**`kappa_sq`**: unchanged between plug-in and marginal — conjugate
$\text{InvGamma}(c + H/2,\, d + \|\Gamma_{r\cdot}\|^2/2)$ with effective
$n = H = 20$; no closed-form marginal correction exists.

**Caveats.**

* Lambda and M are identified only up to an orthogonal rotation of the $k$
  latent axes. Coverage against truth requires Procrustes alignment (uses truth)
  or rotation-invariant summaries such as $\Lambda\Lambda^\top$.
* `sigma_sq` and `kappa_sq` for latent rows $r=q+1,\dots,d$ are
  rotation-affected; reported for completeness only.
* The $\rho_j^2$ surrogate in the plug-in CI is a Gaussian-probit approximation
  ($\sigma_{\text{probit}} = 1.702$) to the exact Schur complement.
